item.title: ‘Verifying authenticity’: DRDO sources on report claiming DRDO data put on dark web
item.description: Sensitive Defence Research and Development Organisation data was reportedly offered for sale. This alleged data was advertised for eight thousand dollars on the dark web. A cyber intelligence firm discovered the sensitive information during routine monitoring. The Defence Research and Development Organisation is currently verifying the authenticity of these claims. Cybersecurity specialists urge immediate forensic verification of the alleged data breach.

item.title: End to Parliament impasse in sight, Lok Sabha may take up bill on exam reforms today
item.description: Parliamentary proceedings may resume Tuesday after Lok Sabha Speaker's outreach to break impasse. The government's bill on paper leaks is likely to be discussed in the lower House. A discussion on the Vande Mataram bill may begin in the Rajya Sabha. Opposition members have moved many amendment notices to the public exams bill. Both sides continued to trade charges while inching towards a resolution.

item.title: India refused to take illegal migrants back as UK didn’t extradite Nirav Modi: Priti Patel
item.description: Former UK Home Secretary Priti Patel stated India refused migrant returns. This refusal was linked to the UK's failure to extradite fugitive jeweler Nirav Modi. Patel expressed dismay that Modi remained in London for seven years. She believes India was angry over Britain's stance on his extradition. India has denied opposing the return of illegal migrants.

item.title: Ayodhya Ram mandir donation row: On SC suggestion, SIT to include a forensic auditor
item.description: The Supreme Court has directed the UP government to add a forensic audit expert to the SIT. This special investigation team will probe alleged embezzlement of Ayodhya Ram Mandir donations. The court wants an expeditious, fair, and transparent investigation into all aspects. item.description: Snap co-founder Evan Spiegel and Miranda Kerr have donated $550 million to erase medical debt. The funds will be channeled through Undue Medical Debt, a prominent organization. This initiative targets vulnerable residents, alleviating burdens of unpayable medical bills.

item.title: Libbie Mugrabi’s Hamptons mansion heads to auction after price cuts
item.description: Socialite Libbie Mugrabi's luxury Bridgehampton mansion is set to be sold in a rare court-ordered public auction after repeated attempts to sell the property privately failed. The auction follows a legal dispute over an unpaid $3.5 million loan secured against the estate. The property, originally listed for $25 million and later reduced to $19 million, will open for bidding at $11 million on August 28.

item.title: Scientists made seabirds fly harder. Only 67% returned next year
item.description: Researchers clipped a few wing and tail feathers of wild black-legged kittiwakes in Alaska to make flying more energy-intensive and tracked them for several years. The birds struggled to raise chicks during that breeding season, and fewer survived to return the next year. However, those that did return migrated farther and were more likely to breed successfully, showing how energy spent in one season can affect the next.

item.title: From pacifist to talks of going nuclear: China shaken as Japan breaks 80-yr-old shackles
item.description: Japan is shifting away from its long-standing pacifist security doctrine, with increasing defense budgets and a major enhancement of military skills. The nation has restarted arms exports and is forming a dedicated intelligence agency. China perceives these changes as a profound provocation and an emerging strategy, sparked by modern threats and regional shifts in the geopolitical landscape.

item.title: Pickaxe Mountain revives the Kahuta question: Could India have hit Pakistan’s nuclear leap?
item.description: The West Asia conflict highlights Iran’s nuclear ambitions and US-Israeli efforts to block them. Pickaxe Mountain, housing hidden nuclear facilities, has become a focal point. Strikes on Natanz in 2025 echoed earlier pre-emptive attacks on nuclear programmes worldwide, from Allied raids on Germany’s heavy-water plant in WWII to Israel’s operations against Iraq’s Osiraq reactor (1981) and Syria’s al-Kibar site (2007). India, however, refrained from striking Pakistan’s Kahuta facility in the 1980s, a decision that enabled Pakistan’s nuclearisation. To avoid escalation, India and Pakistan signed a 1988 accord prohibiting attacks on nuclear sites. India now prioritises survivability through layered missile defence projects.
item.dc:creator: DHRUV YADAV
